facts.fact: CINX, the Cape Town Internet Exchange run by INX-ZA, is in service with 122 connected networks on 153 ports across six Cape Town data-centre locations, per INX-ZA's IX-F member export of 10 August 2026; two new OADC nodes (Rondebosch, Bellville) went live per its 3 August 2026 announcement.
JINX, INX-ZA's Johannesburg exchange, is in service with 208 networks on 289 ports across 9 facilities, per INX-ZA's IX-F member export of 10 August 2026.

Microsoft, Cloudflare, Akamai, Meta and Fastly hold 100 Gbps ports at CINX Cape Town (Teraco Rondebosch), and Amazon holds 100 Gbps at Africa Data Centres Diep Rivier, per INX-ZA's member export of 10 August 2026.
Content delivery network CDN77 has joined JINX Johannesburg as a new member since March 2026, per the article.
South Africa has two exchanges in different cities run by INX-ZA: CINX in Cape Town (122 networks) and JINX in Johannesburg (208 networks), per INX-ZA's member export of 10 August 2026.

note: Port capacities (3,897 Gbps CINX, 10,132 Gbps JINX) are provisioned capacity, not traffic, so no traffic fact.
